source.title: The Architecture of Debt
source.summary: What is a bond? How did debt become the operating system of modern civilization? And why did Islamic scholars see the structural flaw centuries ago?
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: A bond is the simplest thing in finance: a promise to pay back more than you borrowed. But when governments, corporations, and households all run on these promises, you've built a civilization on debt. The global bond market is $130 trillion, dwarfing the stock market, and yet most people never think about it. This episode starts from scratch: what bonds are, how they work, why governments issue them, and how this creates a system where debt isn't just tolerated but required. Al-Ghazali warned that money should facilitate exchange, not generate returns on its own. Ibn Khaldun observed that empires collapse when their debts outgrow their productive capacity. The foundation of the modern financial system is built on something Islamic scholars identified as structurally flawed over 700 years ago.
